## props.kt { #props-kt }

The `prop` / `rootProp` macro pair — the typed, inheritable box-property slot.

`prop` and `rootProp` exist only as the declarations that make `prop<Int>(foo)` resolve; neither
is meant to run, and calling one throws `MacroRegistry.MacroNotExpandedException`. The real work
happens at expansion time in `macro_prop` and `macro_root_prop`, which are handed the type
argument and the name, and return an `Insert` that rewrites the call site to the bare name (or
`root.name`) and pushes two declarations into the box's preamble: a
`var Box.<name> by Inheritance<T>()` and a `val Once.<name> by Onceing<T>()`. Both generated
lines carry the trailing empty-comment marker that makes the preamble gather copy them down into
child boxes, and an import for `T` is added via `kotlinImportStatementFor`. `macro_root_prop`
differs only in targeting `this.root`, so the accessors land on the document root rather than
on the calling box.

## stdlib.kt { #stdlib-kt }

The general-purpose helpers that every Field box already has in scope.

Box code is compiled with `import afield.stdlib.*` in its preamble and with `Box` as an
implicit receiver, so everything here — including the `Box.` extensions — can be called
unqualified from inside a box.

The substantial part is the property-delegate machinery that `prop` and `@exported` generate
against: [`Delegation`](workspace.md#stdlib-kt-delegation) (stores on the receiver's own property bag), [`Inheritance`](workspace.md#stdlib-kt-inheritance) (walks up
`parents` until some ancestor has the property, otherwise throws
[`MissingInheritedPropertyException`](workspace.md#stdlib-kt-missinginheritedpropertyexception) with a message naming the property and the box), and
[`InheritanceFromContext`](workspace.md#stdlib-kt-inheritancefromcontext) (same walk, but prefers each box's live Kotlin variables over raw
properties).

The rest is deliberately small conveniences: graph access (`named`, `+=` / `-=` for
connect/disconnect, `__m` markers); execution control (`begin`, `end`, `start`, `animate`,
`aside`, `cell`); frame-presentation logging (`frameLogStart`, `frameLogStop`,
`frameLogMark`, `frameLogLine`); matrix and buffer building (`mat4`, `mat3`, `FloatBuffer.add`,
`IntBuffer.add`, `ByteBuffer.putf16`); and terse numeric/collection/string shorthands
(`Number.f` / `.i` / `.l` / `.d`, `fa`, `ia`, `Int.alphas`, `String.times`, `List.m` / `.s`,
`String.r`, and `highlightSyntax` behind `String.h` / `String.ss`).

| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">operator</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">get</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">range</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">IntRange</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `list[2..5]` — a new list of the elements in that **inclusive** range, Python-slice syntax with Kotlin's range semantics. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nc">ByteBuffer</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">putf16</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ByteBuffer</span></code> | Appends `value` as a 16-bit half float, **little-endian**, two bytes, and returns the buffer for chaining. |

### Top-level values { #stdlib-kt-values }

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">&#95;currentlyExecutingFragment</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | True while this box is running a *fragment* — a selected region or an `alt-return` block — rather than its whole body. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Number</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">f</span></code> | This number as a `Float` — `3.d.f`, `x.f` — the shorthand that keeps Kotlin's numeric conversions out of the way in graphics code. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Number</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">i</span></code> | This number as an `Int`, **truncated** toward zero: `1.9.i` is 1 and `(-1.9).i` is -1. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">i</span></code> | This `Long` as an `Int`, wrapping silently if it does not fit — the low 32 bits, not a clamp. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Number</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">l</span></code> | This number as a `Long`, truncated toward zero if it was fractional. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">Number</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">d</span></code> | This number as a `Double`. Widening, so nothing is lost — except that a `Float`'s error comes with it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">h</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | This string `highlightSyntax`-ed — HTML-escaped with numbers and punctuation span-wrapped. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">ss</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Alias for `String.h`: this string `highlightSyntax`-ed, ready to print into a box output. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">m</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MutableList</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | This list as a `MutableList` — a **copy**, so editing it leaves the original alone. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">s</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Set</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | This list as a `Set`, dropping duplicates and keeping first-seen order. A copy. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">r</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Regex</span></code> | This string compiled as a `Regex` — `"\\d+".r`. |

### HasMatrix4f { #stdlib-kt-hasmatrix4f }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">interface</span> <span class="nc">HasMatrix4f</span></code>

Implemented by anything that can hand out a 4×4 transform, so callers can take a pose without caring how it was stored.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">m</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Matrix4f</span></code> | This object's transform as a 4×4 matrix. May be recomputed on every read. |

### Delegation { #stdlib-kt-delegation }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">Delegation</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">onGet</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">HasProperties</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">currentValue</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Unit</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">hook</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">inside</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">HasProperties</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">currentValue</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">incomingValue</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">defaultValue</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

The property delegate behind `prop` and `@exported`: reads and writes go to the receiver's own property bag under the property's name, not to a Kotlin field.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">onGet</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">HasProperties</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">currentValue</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Unit</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">?</span></code> |  |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">hook</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">inside</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">HasProperties</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">currentValue</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">incomingValue</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">?</span></code> |  |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">defaultValue</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">?</span></code> |  |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">operator</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">getValue</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">f</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">HasProperties</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">property</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">KProperty</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="o">&#42;</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">T</span></code> | Reads the property from `f`'s bag, filling in `defaultValue` on the first read if it is unset. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">operator</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">setValue</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">f</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">HasProperties</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">property</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">KProperty</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="o">&#42;</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">v</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Writes the property into `f`'s bag, after letting `hook` rewrite the incoming value. |

### MissingInheritedPropertyException { #stdlib-kt-missinginheritedpropertyexception }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">MissingInheritedPropertyException</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">message</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">IllegalStateException</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">message</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

Thrown when an inherited (`prop`-style) property has no value anywhere up the box graph and no default.

### Inheritance { #stdlib-kt-inheritance }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">Inheritance</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">defaultValue</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">T</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

The property delegate that makes a value *inherited*: reading it looks in this box, then breadth-first up through `parents` until some ancestor has it.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">operator</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">getValue</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">f</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">property</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">KProperty</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="o">&#42;</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">T</span></code> | The value from this box or the nearest ancestor that has it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">operator</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">setValue</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">f</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">HasHierarchy</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">property</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">KProperty</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="o">&#42;</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">v</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Writes the value **locally**, shadowing any ancestor's value rather than modifying it. |

### InheritanceFromContext { #stdlib-kt-inheritancefromcontext }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">InheritanceFromContext</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">defaultValue</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">T</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

[`Inheritance`](workspace.md#stdlib-kt-inheritance), but it can also see the *live Kotlin variables* of the boxes it walks — so a plain `val speed = 3.0` in a parent box is inheritable, with no property or annotation needed.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">operator</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">getValue</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">f</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">property</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">KProperty</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="o">&#42;</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">T</span></code> | The value from this box or the nearest ancestor, preferring live Kotlin variables over properties. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">operator</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">setValue</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">f</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">HasHierarchy</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">property</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">KProperty</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="o">&#42;</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">v</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">T</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Writes the value **locally** as a raw property, shadowing whatever an ancestor had. |

### Marker { #stdlib-kt-marker }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">Marker</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">box</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">HasProperties</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">HasHierarchy</span></code>

A named property bag attached to a box — somewhere to hang state that belongs to *part* of a box rather than to the box itself.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">properties</span></code> | This marker's state, as a plain map. In memory only; nothing here is persisted with the document. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">setPropertyRaw</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Any</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">doResync</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Stores a value under `name`. The `doResync` flag is ignored — a marker has no client to notify. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">getPropertyRaw</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">default</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Any</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Any</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The value stored under `name`, or `default` if this marker has never been given one. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">children</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MutableSet</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Always empty: a marker is a leaf. Assigning to it does nothing. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">parents</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MutableSet</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Just the owning box, so a parent walk reaches it. Assigning to it does nothing. |

### Vec2h { #stdlib-kt-vec2h }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">typealias</span> <span class="nc">Vec2h</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">afield</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">four</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">util</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Vec2h</span></code>

A pair of 16-bit half floats, for packed vertex attributes and uniforms. Half the bytes of a [`Vec2`](math.md#linalg-kt-vec2), a fraction of the precision — see `ByteBuffer.putf16` for the range.

### Vec3h { #stdlib-kt-vec3h }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">typealias</span> <span class="nc">Vec3h</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">afield</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">four</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">util</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Vec3h</span></code>

Three 16-bit half floats — the packed transit form of a `Vec3` for GPU buffers.

### Vec4h { #stdlib-kt-vec4h }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">typealias</span> <span class="nc">Vec4h</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">afield</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">four</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">util</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Vec4h</span></code>

Four 16-bit half floats — the packed transit form of a [`Vec4`](math.md#linalg-kt-vec4), and enough precision for a colour.
